front.title: Message Binding for Workload Proof Tokens

abstract.t: The WIMSE Workload Proof Token (WPT) proves possession of a workload's key for an HTTP request and binds the tokens that travel with it. Agent protocols increasingly carry their messages over other transports, such as Media over QUIC, WebSocket, or QUIC streams, often through intermediaries that terminate TLS, such as relays, message brokers, or gateways. There, a proof has no HTTP request to bind to, and the intermediaries that forward a message do not verify it, so freshness has to be established by the receiving verifier. This document defines how a WPT is used with a message that carries it, adds a claim that binds the proof to the content of that message and a claim that echoes a nonce supplied by the verifier, and defines a registry of message canonicalization profiles, with a profile for JSON messages. The same claims can be used in an SD-JWT Key Binding JWT.
